Inside the Trump Campaign to Tame Higher Education

Michael C. BenderThe Trump White House counts its pressure campaign on universities, which has targeted at least 75 schools with investigations, as one of its most successful domestic policy pursuits.

Michael C. BenderBy pairing investigations with pre-emptive funding freezes, the administration has forced college leaders to choose between holding the line on academic freedom and confronting the costs of resistance.

Michael C. BenderThe ferocity of Trump’s attacks blindsided academic leaders, and higher education’s response was uneven. Harvard and labor groups sued. Other universities quietly negotiated. Most hoped Trump wouldn’t notice their schools.

Michael C. BenderHarvard chose to fight and has been targeted with 13 federal investigations. Other schools, fearing a similar backlash from the administration, have adjusted campus policies in hopes of appeasing federal officials.

Michael C. BenderBut Trump’s tactics cost him potential allies: Few university leaders felt they could publicly back the White House because so many Trump demands seemed to undermine higher education, not fix it.
